articles.title: Rybakina estrena su condición de nº1 con una derrota ante la número 118 y se tomará una semana de descanso
articles.standfirst: Alina Charaeva protagoniza la sorpresa del WTA de Pekín y la kazaja anuncia que "es momento de descansar" para recuperarse del pie izquierdo
articles.summary: Alina Charaeva protagoniza la sorpresa del WTA de Pekín y la kazaja anuncia que "es momento de descansar" para recuperarse del pie izquierdo
articles.body: Ha saltado la sorpresa en el 'National Tennis Center' de Pekín. Elena Rybakina, que estrenaba su condición como reina del circuito femenino desde que firmara su pase a las semifinales del US Open, ha caído derrotada a manos de la armenia Alina Charaeva (118 del mundo) por 3-6, 6-4 y 6-3 en la segunda ronda del WTA 1000 asiático. Desde 1975, la nacida en Samara se ha convertido en la jugadora de menor ranking en remontar a una número 1. En dos horas y 12 minutos el público de la 'Diamond Court' se ha quedado sin la máxima favorita al título. La joven de 24 años le dio la vuelta al set y 'break' de la kazaja. La seguridad al primer servicio de Alina fue lo que la impulsó. Ganó el 76% de los puntos que disputó con este. La derrota puso fin a una racha de catorce victorias consecutivas de Rybakina en sus estrenos en torneos WTA 1000. La armenia buscará prolongar su semana mágica en la capital china ante la británica Sonay Kartal (129). Tras caer eliminada, la campeona del grande neoyorquino anunció unos días de descanso para poder recuperarse de las molestias que sufre en el pie izquierdo, y que la obligaron a jugar bajo los efectos de analgésicos en las pistas de Flushing Meadows: "Noté un poco el pie al final del partido, así que es momento de descansar un poco y ver qué viene en las próximas semanas", señalaba. "Pasaron muchas cosas después de la victoria en el Abierto de Estados Unidos. No tuve muchas oportunidades de dormir y recuperarme", afirmó Rybakina, pagando el cansancio de una temporada larga. Tampoco pudo ayudar a su país en las finales de la Billie Jean King Cup. No ha querido precisar próximas citas, aunque figura apuntada en el WTA 1000 de Wuhan (12 al 18 de octubre), segundo torneo de la categoría en la gira asiática femenina.

articles.title: John McEnroe names the American man he thinks has the best chance of winning a Grand Slam title
articles.summary: John McEnroe loves American tennis and has maintained that mindset even well into his retirement. As a player, he never missed a Davis Cup match,...
articles.body:
John McEnroe loves American tennis and has maintained that mindset even well into his retirement.

As a player, he never missed a Davis Cup match, referencing some of those triumphs among the best of his entire storied career.

Then, once he stopped playing, the 67-year-old took up the mantle of Davis Cup captain, resigning after just 14 months, as he failed to get regular commitments from the stars of the era like Pete Sampras and Andre Agassi.

Now a prominent and outspoken pundit, he continues to fly the flag proudly when given the opportunity.

Speaking as a Eurosport and TNT Sports pundit recently, John McEnroe has now named the American man he thinks is the closest to claiming a Grand Slam title.

John McEnroe previews the future of men's tennis in America

It has been 23 long years since we last saw a US man lift a major, although we came close just last month when Ben Shelton reached the US Open final.

Sadly, he failed to challenge Alexander Zverev, but it marked a huge breakthrough for the 23-year-old.

This likely prompted McEnroe's choice, as he noted: "People ask me all the time when we are going to get an American winning a Grand Slam and I put Ben (Shelton) at the top of the list.

"We wait to see what happens with players like (Jakub) Mensik or [Joao] Fonseca and whether these young kids can get over the hump and challenge Sinner and Alcaraz.

"Or will Sascha Zverev be dominant and win a few more Grand Slams over the next few years?

"Carlos and Jannik were a long way ahead of the rest for the last couple of years and injuries have stopped that this year, so it's an interesting question moving forward who will step up."

Then, discussing the wider topic of American tennis, he feared for participation, with other sports seemingly taking precedent and thus hoovering up the elite athletes.

McEnroe added: "It feels to me that tennis is more accessible in other countries, especially Europe.

"In our country, to be blunt, the accessibility is a big issue. The best athletes play American football, basketball, in some cases, soccer. You have the affordability issues and tennis is expensive."

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: India’s biggest hits and flops - from historic golf gold to tennis medal drought
articles.summary: India signed off from the Asian Games 2026 in fourth place with 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.
articles.body: India signed off from the Asian Games 2026 in fourth place with 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. The final tally was below the record 106 medals won at Hangzhou, but a strong finish in the final days changed the complexion of the campaign.From Kumkum Mohod’s historic archery gold and Aman Sehrawat’s wrestling triumph to disappointing campaigns in tennis and some traditionally strong disciplines, India’s Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games journey had its share of soaring highs and hard misses.Here are India's biggest hits and flops from Aichi-Nagoya.The Hits1. Archery: The biggest gold-medal successArchery was arguably India's biggest success story when it came to gold medals.India won five gold medals, with the women's and men's compound teams, mixed compound team, women's recurve team and Kumkum Mohod's individual recurve triumph providing the highlights.The biggest moment came from 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod, who became the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve gold at the Asian Games.Her success, along with the women's recurve team's gold, gave Indian archery a memorable Games. Kumkum also added a silver in the mixed recurve team event with Dhiraj Bommadevara.2. Hockey: Two golds and Olympic qualificationIndian hockey delivered when it mattered most.The women's team ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games gold, while Harmanpreet Singh's men's team defeated Malaysia 5-1 in the final to retain the title.The two victories also had an Olympic dimension, with India's performances securing qualification opportunities for Los Angeles 2028.The men's final was the perfect way to close India's medal campaign, with the 5-1 victory delivering the country's 21st gold.3. Cricket: Both teams defend their titlesIndia's cricket teams delivered two more gold medals.The women's team retained its title, while the men's side defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the final to successfully defend India's Asian Games crown. Abhishek Sharma's explosive batting and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 were among the highlights of the men's final.The men's final also became one of the most talked-about sporting moments of the Games, thanks to the India-Pakistan rivalry.4. Boxing: Three goldsIndia's boxers produced one of the strongest late surges of the Games, winning three gold medals.Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal emerged as champions in their respective categories.For Lovlina, the victory was particularly significant: she became only the second Indian woman after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing gold.5. Wrestling: Aman Sehrawat's comebackAman Sehrawat's gold was one of the more compelling individual stories of the Games.The wrestler had endured a difficult period involving illness, absences and a loss of motivation following the Paris Olympics. His return to the top at Aichi-Nagoya turned the campaign into a personal comeback story as well as a medal-winning one.India finished with two wrestling golds, along with silver and bronze medals.6. Pranavi Urs makes golf historyPranavi Urs created history by winning India's first women's individual golf gold at the Asian Games.India also took silver in the women's team event, making golf one of the country's notable success stories in Aichi-Nagoya.7. Kabaddi: India keep its Asian Games dominanceKabaddi remained one of India's most dependable gold-medal sports at Aichi-Nagoya.Both the men's and women's teams won gold, allowing India to retain its titles and reinforce its dominance in the sport at the Asian Games.The double triumph was another strong performance from a discipline where India continues to set the continental benchmark.8. Athletics: India's biggest medal contributorAthletics was India's biggest contributor by overall medal count, producing 24 medals.The medal haul included silver medals for Ancy Sojan, Sarvesh Kushare, Sawan Berwal, Gulveer Singh and others, along with multiple bronze medals across track and field.The sport also produced historic moments, including Baranica Elangovan's first-ever Asian Games pole-vault medal for India and Vithya Ramraj's national-record bronze in the 400m hurdles.The caveat is the gold count. Athletics produced a huge volume of medals but only one gold, meaning the sport's conversion into top-of-the-podium finishes remains an area India will want to improve.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyThe Flops1. Tennis: A historic medal droughtTennis was arguably India's biggest disappointment.For the first time in four decades, India failed to win a single Asian Games tennis medal. The campaign ended without a podium finish despite the country's historically strong record in the sport at the continental event.The result was particularly striking because tennis has traditionally been one of India's reliable Asian Games medal sports.2. Shooting: Too many near misses before the turnaroundShooting eventually contributed 15 medals, including three golds, making it one of India's biggest medal-producing sports.But the campaign began with considerable disappointment.India endured several fourth-place finishes and missed opportunities before Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet finally ended the wait for a shooting gold.Tilottama Sen and Vidarsa Vinod, for example, finished fourth and fifth respectively in the women's 50m rifle 3P individual final.The final medal count was impressive, but expectations around India's shooters were even higher.3. Badminton: Below expectationsBadminton managed only one medal — a bronze in the men's team event.The result was underwhelming for a sport that has produced some of India's biggest Asian Games and Olympic stars.The campaign was also overshadowed by criticism of the Games' scheduling and organisation. H.S. Prannoy, who won the men's team bronze, described the experience as “sad” for athletes and criticised the accommodation and scheduling arrangements.4. Equestrian: A quiet disappointmentEquestrian was another discipline that failed to make a mark for India at Aichi-Nagoya.Despite India's pedigree in the sport and its strong performances at previous Asian Games, the contingent returned without a medal.The result added to a list of disciplines where India was unable to convert participation and experience into podium finishes, making equestrian a relatively disappointing campaign.5. Table tennis, fencing, esports, rowing all disappointSeveral disciplines failed to make a significant impact for India at the Asian Games 2026. Esports was among the clearest disappointments, with India failing to win a medal across its events, while fencing and volleyball also ended without a podium finish despite sizeable contingents and expectations.Table tennis managed only one bronze, a modest return for a sport with India’s growing international stature, making it another underwhelming campaign.Rowing produced a solitary bronze, leaving the discipline with a relatively limited medal haul. articles.title: El 'qualy' Munar se cuela en Tokio en su octava semifinal del circuito
articles.standfirst: El mallorquín cede sólo seis juegos en los cuartos con el francés Jacquet
articles.summary: El mallorquín cede sólo seis juegos en los cuartos con el francés Jacquet
articles.body: El tenis masculino español ya tiene a un representante en las semifinales del Open 500 de Tokio. Se trata de Jaume Munar, que ha dado buena cuenta este domingo de Kyryan Jacquet, por 6-4 y 6-2, en apenas 1 hora y 40 minutos. Munar, el 64 del ranking y procedente de la previa, se cuela en la primera semifinal de la presente temporada y la octava de su carrera. Es el sexto jugador que llega tan lejos en el certamen como 'qualy'. Para encontrar la última vez que estuvo entre los cuatro mejores de un torneo del circuito había que remontarse a Basilea 2025. El mallorquín, de 29 años, espera en la penúltima ronda del lunes al ganador del cruce de cuartos entre su compatriota Carlos Alcaraz y Denis Shapovalov. La victoria del murciano aseguraría la presencia de un miembro de la Armada' en la final. Munar acumula ya cinco partidos ganados en la capital japonesa. Desde la fase clasificatoria, ha dejado por el camino a nombres como Taylor Fritz, que era el tercer cabeza de serie del certamen. Jaume ha ascendido ya 15 posiciones en las listas. Es virtualmente el número 49. Su temporada ha estado marcada por la lesión en el brazo en los cuartos de Rotterdam ante Alexander Bublik que le privó de estar después en Doha, Dubái, y los tres primeros Masters 1000 del calendario: Indian Wells, Miami y Montecarlo.

articles.title: Alcaraz pasa otra ronda por la retirada de Shapovalov y asegura un español en la final de Tokio
articles.standfirst: El murciano, verdugo del canadiense, se las verá este lunes con su compatriota Munar
articles.summary: El murciano, verdugo del canadiense, se las verá este lunes con su compatriota Munar
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz lo ha vuelto a hacer. Por tercer día consecutivo, ha firmado una remontada en Tokio para encadenar presencias en las semifinales, igualando a Rafael Nadal. Este lo hizo en 2010 y 2011. Alcaraz, primer favorito del certamen, ha acabado este domingo con la dura resistencia de Denis Shapovalov, por 7-6(3), 2-1 y retirada del canadiense por lesión. El vencedor se acordó del adversario en su firma a la cámara: "Regresa pronto Denis". Un gesto que le engrandece aún más. El duelo fratricida en la semifinal con Jaume Munar asegura la presencia de un español en la final por séptima vez desde 1972. Además de Alcaraz, vigente campeón, se plantaron en la lucha por el título Manolo Orantes (1975 y 1977); David Ferrer (2007) y Nadal (2010-11). "Es todo de cabeza, vas a ir a más", le decía su entrenador Samuel López desde el banquillo. Carlitos parecía haber hecho ya lo más difícil: levantar un 2-4, un 3-5 y un 4-5 y pelota de set. En esa situación se sacó una dejada de la chistera. Servía con 6-5 para cerrar la manga inicial. Lo que pasa es que las dudas al servicio del tenista de El Palmar las aprovechó Shapovalov para romper por tercera vez el saque de su rival y llevar el desenlace a la muerte súbita. La grada de la central del Ariake Coliseum no disimulaba sus colores. La muerte súbita fue un punto de inflexión en el partido. El campeón de siete grandes había tomado ventaja a pesar de los 29 puntos perdidos al saque. Con 1-0 en la continuación, al canadiense le tuvieron que atender en los vestuarios a la altura de la cadera. Denis, el 46 del ranking a sus 27 años, hace tiempo que no acostumbra a jugar duelos de tanta intensidad. Estuvo en pista dos juegos más antes de sacar la bandera blanca. Había transcurrido una hora y 22 minutos desde el inicio. Ya son 40 las victorias de Alcaraz contra zurdos por 12 derrotas. De los 14 jugadores que responden a ese perfil en el 'top100' no hay ninguno más con vida en Tokio. "Estoy lejos de donde quiero estar, pero estoy haciendo las cosas bien fuera de la pista porque estoy entrenando bien. Los próximos partidos y torneos los voy a utilizar para sentirme mejor", reflexionaba el número tres mundial. Otro zurdo, Ben Shelton, que acechaba al español en el ranking tras su final en el US Open, está hoy a 580 puntos. El estadounidense se borró de Tokio y falta ver si estará en condiciones de reaparecer en el Masters 1000 de Shanghái. La regularidad adquirida por Carlitos con el paso del tiempo se demuestra en la estadística. Son seis campañas seguidas con un mínimo de 30 partidos ganados a pesar de que en 2026 se perdió más de cuatro meses de competición por la muñeca.

articles.standfirst: El murciano domina los precedentes entre ambos por tres victorias a una
articles.summary: El murciano domina los precedentes entre ambos por tres victorias a una
articles.body: El tenis masculino español tendrá este martes la posibilidad de lograr el sexto título de la presente temporada y el segundo en la gira asiática después del logrado el pasado martes por Alejandro Davidovich en Chengdu. El duelo fratricida de este lunes entre Carlos Alcaraz y Jaume Munar en las semifinales del Open 500 de Tokio garantiza la presencia de un miembro de la Armada en la última ronda. Además de Alcaraz, campeón la pasada edición, otros tres españoles jugaron por la corona en la capital japonesa: Manolo Orantes (1975 y 1977), David Ferrer (2007) y Rafael Nadal (2010-11). Los tres llegaron a levantar el trofeo. Carlitos y Munar han jugado cuatro veces en el circuito y el murciano domina los precedentes por tres triunfos a uno. La victoria del mallorquín llegó en el primer cara a cara entre ambos, en las semifinales de Marbella 2021. La primera semifinal de Tokio entre Carlos Alcaraz y Jaume Munar se celebrará este lunes, en la central del Ariake Coliseum, a partir de las 09.00 horas en España. El partido de semifinales del Open 500 de Tokio entre Carlos Alcaraz y Jaume Munar se podrá seguir en España a través de Movistar+, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición. Además habrá una amplia información del torneo en MARCA.com y Radio MARCA.

articles.standfirst: El murciano dejó un bonito detalle tras la lesión del canadiense y que le hizo abandonar
articles.summary: El murciano dejó un bonito detalle tras la lesión del canadiense y que le hizo abandonar
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz es el jugador más querido y admirado en los vestuarios del circuito profesional de tenis por detalles como el que dejó en los cuartos de Tokio. Tras pasa a las semifinales por la retirada de Denis Shapovalov a la conclusión del tercer juego del segundo set, el murciano no pasó por alto el problema físico que había obligado a decir adiós antes de tiempo al norteamericano. "Regresa pronto Denis", firmó en la cámara del torneo japonés. Otro gesto que le engrandece aún más. Hasta el momento del abandono Shapovalov había presentado una dura batalla al vigente campeón e incluso dispuso de una pelota de set, con 5-4. No es la primera vez que el joven de El Palmar tiene un gesto de estas características para sus compañeros de profesión. La pasada campaña, tras no poder continuar Jannik Sinner en la final del Masters 1000 de Cincinnati, le mandó un mensaje a través de la cámara: "Lo siento Jannik". El italiano se había sentido indispuesto.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock China Open exit, falls to Nikola Bartunkova in straight sets
articles.summary: World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shock third-round exit at the China Open on Sunday, losing 6-4, 6-3 to Czech Republic’s Nikola Bartunkova.
articles.body: World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shock third-round exit at the China Open on Sunday, losing 6-4, 6-3 to Czech Republic’s Nikola Bartunkova. The 34th-ranked Bartunkova produced one of the biggest upsets of the tournament, defeating the four-time Grand Slam champion in one hour and 34 minutes. The Czech hit four aces and capitalised on Sabalenka’s struggles to close out a straight-sets victory.Sabalenka had five break-point opportunities in the opening set but was unable to convert any of them. Bartunkova, meanwhile, stayed composed on the big points and secured the only break she needed to take the first set 6-4.The Czech continued to dictate the contest in the second set, breaking Sabalenka and maintaining her advantage to close out the match 6-3. The defeat continues Sabalenka’s difficult record at the Beijing tournament. The Belarusian has never progressed beyond the quarterfinals at the China Open.Top two seeds now outSabalenka arrived in Beijing looking to bounce back from her US Open disappointment, where she was denied a third consecutive title by Elena Rybakina. However, Rybakina herself suffered a surprise defeat earlier in Beijing, losing to unseeded Alina Charaeva in the second round.The early exits of the top two seeds mean neither Rybakina nor Sabalenka will feature in the latter stages of the WTA 1000 tournament. The China Open is being played on hard courts in Beijing from September 30 to October 11. Bartunkova will next face Austria’s Sinja Kraus, who defeated Ukraine’s Dayana Yastremska 6-1, 6-4.The Czech will now have an opportunity to extend her breakthrough run in Beijing after taking down one of the tournament’s biggest names.In the men’s draw, top seed Alexander Zverev is scheduled to face Novak Djokovic in the quarterfinals. articles.title: China Open: Aryna Sabalenka stunned by Nikola Bartunkova in Beijing
articles.summary: World number two Aryna Sabalenka follows Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she falls to a surprise defeat by Nikola Bartunkova.
articles.body:
World number two Aryna Sabalenka followed Elena Rybakina out the door at the China Open as she fell to a surprise defeat by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova.

It comes a day after top seed Rybakina, who defeated Sabalenka in last month's US Open final and replaced the Belarusian at the top of the rankings, was knocked out by Armenian world number 118 Alina Charaeva.

Czech Bartunkova sprung another upset at the WTA 1000 tournament and continued her breakthrough season with a 6-4 6-3 over Sabalenka.

"I focused on myself, to be calm," said Bartunkova, who will face Austria's Sinja Kraus next.

"She's a legend, so I'm really happy that I won the match."

It is the first time since 2015 that the top two seeds have failed to reach the round of 16 at the China Open.

Sabalenka has not won a title since completing the 'Sunshine Double' in March, when she triumped at Indian Wells and the Miami Open back-to-back.

It has been a mixed year for Sabalenka by her high standards. She will finish without a Grand Slam trophy for the first time since 2022 and has often struggled to control her frustrations on court.

Against Bartunkova, she failed to convert any of her five break points and she threw her racquet after falling a break down early in the second set.

Kartal wins again as Zverev sets up Djokovic tie

At the Japan Open, Carlos Alcaraz reached the semi-finals after Denis Shapovalov retired with an injury to his right thigh.

Alcaraz, the defending champion in Tokyo, saved a set point in the opening set and was leading 7-6 (7-3) 2-1 when the Canadian was forced to withdraw.

It is just Alcaraz's third event since returning from a wrist injury at last month's US Open, where he fell to Ben Shelton in the quarter-finals.

He will face fellow Spaniard Jaume Munar for a place in the final.

articles.title: China Open: Aryna Sabalenka suffers shock Beijing exit — a day after new world No 1 Elena Rybakina was knocked out
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka exits the Beijing tournament in straight sets against Czech teenager Nikola Bartunkova, while Carlos Alcaraz advances in Tokyo; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Czech 20-year-old Nikola Bartunkova defeated the four-time Grand Slam champion 6-4 6-3, leaving the tournament without its two top seeds in the opening week.

Rybakina was knocked out on Saturday, and Sabalenka has now joined her in an early exit from the WTA 1000 event in Beijing.

Sabalenka, who was denied a US Open three-peat by Rybakina last month, squandered five break points in the opening set as her struggles in Beijing continued.

The 28-year-old Belarusian has never progressed beyond the quarter-finals at the tournament.

Bartunkova, the No 26 seed, will next face Austria's 24-year-old Sinja Kraus, who defeated Dayana Yastremska 6-1 6-4 earlier on Sunday.

Fifth seed Mirra Andreeva eased into the fourth round with a 6-4 6-1 victory over Polina Kudermetova.

The French Open champion fired six aces and converted five of seven break-point opportunities to overwhelm her Uzbek opponent in just 68 minutes.

Top seed Carlos Alcaraz advanced to the semi-finals of the Japan Open after Denis Shapovalov was forced to retire with a hip injury, extending the Spaniard's strong return from a four-month wrist injury lay-off.

The defending champion was leading 7-6 (7-4) 2-1 when the Canadian called it a day.

"It was a little bit frustrating with my serve. I couldn't find a good way of serving: I was struggling almost every game on serve," Alcaraz said after dropping serve three times in the opening set.

"But I'm just happy with the way I came back after every break. It was a great first set: Great points, great rallies."

The Spaniard said he was disappointed to progress in such circumstances.

"It's a shame that he had to pull out. Going through to a semi-final like this is not the way I wanted, but sometimes sports are tough. You have to accept it. Hopefully he's going to be able to play in Shanghai healthy."

Alcaraz will face compatriot Jaume Munar in the semi-finals after the qualifier defeated France's Kyrian Jacquet 6-4 6-2.

articles.title: Sabalenka, Rybakina handed shock defeats at China Open tennis
articles.summary: The Belarusian’s exit follows top seed Rybakina losing to unseeded Charaeva in her first match as world number one.
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova in the third round of the China Open, leaving the event without its top two seeds as world number one Elena Rybakina was ousted in the second round.

Czech player Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes on Sunday.

“I focused on myself, to be calm,” Bartunkova said.

“She’s a legend … so I’m really happy that I won the match,” she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion.

Bartunkova next faces Austria’s Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.

Second-seeded Sabalenka squandered five chances to break serve in the sixth game of the first set, with Bartunkova strong on defence and firing deep.

The 28-year-old from Belarus threw on a cap for the eighth game of the first set as the women switched between playing in the shade and the sun, but it did not turn the tide in her favour.

A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.

Earlier on Saturday, Elena Rybakina – who replaced Sabalenka as the world number one last month – was ousted by Alina Charaeva in the second round.

Top seed Alexander Zverev was scheduled to play Novak Djokovic later on Sunday in the quarterfinals of the men’s 500-level event also taking place.

The 39-year-old Serbian great enters the match with an extraordinary unbeaten streak in Beijing, but Zverev — last month’s US Open champion — is in the running for the top men’s ranking.

articles.summary: La bielorrusa pierde ante la checa Nikola Bartunkova (número 34 del mundo) por 6-4 y 6-3
articles.body: La bielorrusa Aryna Sabalenka (número 2 del ranking de la WTA), segunda favorita, perdió este domingo ante la checa Nikola Bartunkova (número 34) por 6-4 y 6-3 en tercera ronda del Abierto de China, que se quedó sin sus dos principales cabezas de serie en poco más de doce horas. A Sabalenka no le funcionó su saque y, de hecho, ganó más puntos con su segundo servicio (63%) que con el primero (53%). Además perdió hasta tres veces su saque y no logró ningún break. La bielorrusa empezó el partido perdiendo su saque y en el sexto juego desperdició hasta cinco puntos de rotura, los únicos que tendría a lo largo del encuentro, que duró una hora y 35 minutos sobre la pista central Diamond del complejo tenístico del torneo pekinés. La eliminación de Sabalenka se sumó a la de la kazaja Elena Rybakina, derrotada el sábado por la armenia Alina Charaeva (número 118) en su primer partido como número uno del mundo.

Sus únicos verdugos son mallorquines. Munar le ganó en sus primeras semifinales en el Open 250 de Marbella, en 2021, y Rafael Nadal le superó en los dos primeros precedentes entre ambos: Madrid 2021 e Indian Wells 2022. Carlitos se ve las caras este lunes por quinta vez con Munar, en las semifinales del Open 500 de Tokio.

articles.summary: El ruso, verdugo del argentino Fran Cerúndolo, se afianza en las posiciones que dan billete a las ATP Finals
articles.body: Daniil Medvedev avanza con paso firme en el Open 500 de Pekín y ya está en las semifinales del certamen por cuarto año seguido, algo que sólo había logrado antes Novak Djokovic (2012-15). El ruso, campeón el martes en Hangzhou, encadena siete victorias en su particular gira por tierras chinas. Nadie ha ganado más que él en superficie dura esta campaña. Y es que ya había levantado antes los trofeos de Brisbane y Dubái para un total de 30 partidos ganados. Su última víctima ha sido este domingo Fran Cerúndolo, por 7-6(4) y 6-3. En la penúltima ronda espera al ganador del partido entre Alexander Zverev (1) y Novak Djokovic (6). Medvedev se afianza como octavo de la Race 2026 que da billete a las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). Suma 3.210 puntos, que son 660 más que Alex de Miñaur, inmediatamente detrás de él. Precisamente el australiano disputará la otra semifinal de Pekín frente a Hubert Hurkacz.

articles.title: Djokovic es imbatible en Pekín: 32-0 y le quita otro récord a Nadal
articles.standfirst: El serbio remonta un set y acaba con el favorito Zverev para sumar siete semifinales en la capital china
articles.summary: El serbio remonta un set y acaba con el favorito Zverev para sumar siete semifinales en la capital china
articles.body: Novak Djokovic es el mejor tenista de la historia aquí y en Pekín. Lo volvió a demostrar este domingo al remontarle un set a Alexander Zverev para pasar a las semifinales del China Open 500 de Pekín por 4-6, 6-4 y 6-4, en 2 horas y 34 minutos. Ya son siete veces entre los cuatro mejores en la capital china para un total de 202 veces a lo largo de su incomparable carrera. El tope lo tiene Jimmy Connors (239) seguido de Roger Federer (211). El serbio se anota un nuevo récord de la Era Open ya que su marca de 32-0 supera la que firmó Rafael Nadal en Roland Garros entre 2005 y 2009. Una derecha mordida de Zverev acabó con otro ejercicio de resistencia de Nole. Djokovic, 10 años mayor que Sascha, rejuvenece cada vez que pisa tierras chinas. A excepción del mes de enero, con su final en el Open de Australia, el serbio ha reconocido sufrir problemas físicos que no le han permitido ofrecer su mejor versión. Nole fue capaz de fabricarse dos pelotas de break en el décimo juego para igualar a cinco (5-4 y 15-40). Las salvó el enorme saque de Zverev. Pudo firma después las tablas en el marcador anotándose el segundo parcial. En el cara o cruz del tercer set, la leyenda de Belgrado fue mejor desde el fondo de la pista. A la segunda pelota de partido, pasó a las semifinales. Se las verá este lunes con Daniil Medvedev. Pase lo que pase, un nuevo récord ya es suyo. Djokovic, que está a un triunfo de regresa al 'top10' en detrimento de Arthur Fils, se mete de lleno en la pelea por uno de los billetes para las ATP Finals de Turín. Es décimo de la Race 2026, a 680 puntos de Medvedev, precisamente su siguiente rival en Pekín.

articles.title: China Open: Novak Djokovic beats top seed Alexander Zverev to reach semi-finals and dents German's bid to finish year as world number one
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic's quest to win a first trophy of 2026 continues with a hard-fought victory in the quarter-finals of the China Open.
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic battled back from a set down to defeat top seed Alexander Zverev and book his place in the China Open semi-finals.

The 39-year-old Serbian triumphed 4-6 6-4 6-4 against world number two Zverev and will play Daniil Medvedev in the last four.

Djokovic's victory over Zverev dented the German's quest to finish the year as the world's number one-ranked player.

"These are the kind of moments that I still play for, compete for," Djokovic said.

"The motivation is big when you are feeling good and competing at par with the best players in the world in front of 15,000 people.

"These are the kind of moments that define dreams, I think, of every tennis player."

Sabalenka stunned by Bartunkova at China Open

In their first meeting in just under 16 months, Djokovic initially struggled to handle Zverev's power, and the 29-year-old secured the first set after capitalising on a break in the first game.

However, Djokovic managed to work his way back into the contest, and the 24-time Grand Slam winner seized an opportunity with a break at 5-4 in the second set to level the match.

Little separated the pair in the third set, but the veteran struck again at 5-4 on Zverev's serve to clinically seal victory.

It took Djokovic's unbeaten tally in Beijing to 32 matches as he moved a step closer to a seventh China Open title and a first trophy of what has been a difficult 2026, with form and fitness proving challenging.

"It's been a struggle this year for different reasons," Djokovic added.

"But I'm still there, still grinding, still making the youngsters work for their money. I'm just glad to push it through."

Djokovic will face third seed Medvedev, who earlier overcame Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7-4) 6-3, on Monday.

Poland's Hubert Hurkacz also progressed to the semi-finals with a 7-6 (7-2) 6-2 win over Karen Khachanov.

He will play Australia's Alex de Minaur who was off the pace in the first set against Andrey Rublev before he stepped up to record a 1-6 6-2 6-3 victory.

articles.title: China Open: Novak Djokovic keeps unblemished record in Beijing by handing Alexander Zverev a rare defeat

articles.body:
The 39-year-old Serbian created a new piece of tennis history with the best start in men's singles at a tour-level event in the Open Era as he moved to 32-0 in Beijing.

With his victory, Djokovic moved past Rafael Nadal for the best start at a single event, with Nadal having won his first 31 matches at the French Open.

Djokovic is a record six-time champion in Beijing and had won all 29 of his previous matches at the tournament before returning this year for the first time since 2015, when he defeated Nadal in the final to claim his sixth title.

"I had a terrible start. Two double faults at the beginning. It was quite cold and honestly, I didn't feel warmed up, but my fault," Djokovic said.

"I gave him an early break and then it was hard to come back in the first set. I had a couple of break points when he was serving for the set at 5-4, but didn't use them, but I kind of felt already from midway through the first set that I was starting to get a good rhythm, at least one my serve and on serve plus one."

Meeting for the first time in ​nearly 16 months, Djokovic struggled to contain the German's power in the early stages as Zverev claimed the ​opening set, but the Serb gradually ⁠worked his way into the ⁠match and refused to let his opponent pull away.

The turning point came late ‌in the second set when Djokovic broke at 5-4 to level the match, shifting the momentum in his ‌favour after a tightly contested battle.

With little separating the pair in the third, the Serbian struck again at 5-4 on the Zverev serve, securing the decisive break ⁠to seal victory.

The pair had not met ​since last year's French Open, where ​Djokovic won in four sets, and this encounter ​again highlighted the Serb's ability to deliver under ⁠pressure despite a season disrupted by physical issues.

With the win, Djokovic moved a step closer to a seventh ⁠China Open title and an elusive ​first trophy of the year, while denying Zverev ​another opportunity to strengthen his bid for the world No 1 ranking.

Djokovic's next assignment will be a meeting with Daniil Medvedev , who earlier overcame Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7-4) 6-3.

He is just the third man in ATP history (since 1973) to earn a top-three win after turning 39 years of age, after Ken Rosewall and Jimmy Connors.

"To be honest, these are the kind of moments that I still play for, compete for," Djokovic said.

"The motivation is big obviously when you are feeling good and competing at par with the best players in the world, in front of 15,000 people of course. These are the kind of moments that define dreams, I think, of every tennis player. It's been a struggle this year, to be honest, for different reasons, but I'm still there, still grinding, still making the youngsters work for their money. I'm just glad to push it through."

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis , former British No 1 Annabel Croft described the match as an "incredible contest".

"Some high-quality, absolutely fantastic tennis between two brilliant players. Why would you ever doubt Novak Djokovic even at the age of 39?

"The match got better and better as well, and had some different tactical shifts for Djokovic, who after the long physical points, I thought his legs were tiring, but he came back. He threw in some drop shots, he threw in some serve and volleys early in the second set and just changed things up with the pattern of play.

"Djokovic came up with the answers. It was on a knife edge right to the end but what a finish and what a treat for all those fans in Beijing."

At the Japan Open, top seed Carlos Alcaraz required only 83 minutes on court before he booked a place in the semi-finals after Denis Shapovalov retired when trailing 7-6 (7-3) 2-1 .

articles.title: Alex de Minaur gives his honest opinion on whether Grand Slams should scrap playing best of five matches
articles.summary: Over the past few weeks, debate over whether best-of-five-set tennis should remain has been almost relentless. Alex de Minaur, as one of the sport’s hardest....
articles.body:
Over the past few weeks, debate over whether best-of-five-set tennis should remain has been almost relentless.

Alex de Minaur, as one of the sport's hardest workers and most athletic players, would seem like a guarantee to fall on the side of the defence.

However, speaking after his latest win, a battling comeback win over Andrey Rublev, when asked to weigh in on the debate, his answer was not so black and white.

Instead, the Aussie offered a nuanced take, considering it from both sides, before delivering his final personal verdict.

Alex de Minaur weighs in on debate surrounding Grand Slams scrapping best of five set tennis

Alex de Minaur began by contextualising this debate, noting: "Look, when you ask me something like that, there's two ways to look at it."

He then admitted: "If I look at it as the player, I don't want to get rid of best-of-five because I believe that that is the history and tradition of our sport, what makes Grand Slams truly unique. We used to have a lot more best-of-five matches. Davis Cup used to be best-of-five. Finals of the Masters used to be best-of-five.

"I understand when you're trying to sell a product, that kind of side of things, that debate.

"If me answering as the player that I am, I would not want to get rid of best-of-five."

Carlos Alcaraz defended best-of-five-set tennis earlier this week, whilst Daniil Medvedev said he would be okay for it to be scrapped , highlighting the variance in opinions amongst the ATP Tour.

Alex de Minaur has a message for his fanbase in China

Since returning to the China Open this year, and admittedly throughout his career, De Minaur has commanded great support from the Chinese fans.

They appreciate great tennis players, and he certainly is one of them.

Speaking in that same press conference where he discussed this best-of-five debate, he was also asked if he had a message for those loyal supporters of his here in Beijing.

He replied: "Yeah, I mean, it is pretty cool to feel the love that I have felt here in China ever since I was very young. Going back to Zhuhai, I've had some great memories over here. I've always felt a lot of love from the Chinese fans. It makes it special coming back here.

"Yeah, I've played some good tennis here over the years. I always feel comfortable."

articles.title: Djokovic defeats top seed Zverev to reach China Open semifinals
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic to face Daniil Medvedev in the semifinals in Beijing after the Russian defeats Francisco Cerundolo.
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic has brushed aside ongoing injury-related struggles and produced a trademark comeback to defeat top seed Alexander Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 for a place in the China Open semifinals, extending his unbeaten record in the tournament.

Playing the ATP 500 event in Beijing for the first time since 2015, the six-time champion was pushed to the limit by reigning French Open and US Open champion Zverev, who delivered 19 aces in the match on Sunday.

Meeting for the first time in nearly 16 months, Djokovic struggled to contain the German’s power in the early stages as the 29-year-old Zverev claimed the opening set, but the Serb gradually worked his way into the match and refused to let his opponent pull away.

“I had a terrible start – two double faults at the beginning. It was quite cold, and honestly, I didn’t feel warmed up, but my fault,” Djokovic said.

“I gave him an early break, and then it was hard to come back in the first set.”

The contest was briefly interrupted by a moment of controversy when Zverev argued that the electronic advertising signage had gone dark during a rally and requested a video review after losing the point.

Replays showed a section of the signage had switched off although not as Zverev was missing the forehand. The chair umpire ordered the point to be replayed, prompting a frustrated exchange from Djokovic.

The turning point came late in the second set when Djokovic broke at 5-4 to level the match, shifting the momentum in his favour after a tightly contested battle.

With little separating the pair in the third, the Serbian struck again at 5-4 on the Zverev serve, securing the decisive break to seal the victory in two hours and 35 minutes.

“I was trying to be aggressive and come to the net and change up the pace, not giving the same pattern,” Djokovic said.

“I am just glad that I held my nerves, played good shots at important moments, 5-4 in the second and third.”

The pair had not met since Roland Garros in 2025, where Djokovic won in four sets, and Sunday’s encounter again highlighted the Serb’s ability to deliver under pressure despite a season disrupted by physical issues.

With the victory, Djokovic moved a step closer to a seventh China Open title and an elusive first trophy of the year while denying Zverev another opportunity to strengthen his bid for the world number one ranking.

Djokovic will face Daniil Medvedev in the semifinals after the Russian defeated Francisco Cerundolo 7-6(4), 6-3 earlier.

Rybakina withdraws from Wuhan after China Open exit

World number one Elena Rybakina withdrew from this month’s Wuhan Open due to a foot injury, tournament organisers said on Sunday, a day after the Kazakh suffered a shock defeat in her opening match at the China Open.

Rybakina, who lost to world number 118 Alina Charaeva in Beijing, said she would take time away from competition to recover.

“I’m very sorry to the fans who were looking forward to seeing me play,” Rybakina said in a story posted on the tournament’s Instagram account.

“I’ll take some time to rest and recover. Thank you for your understanding and continued support.”

The 27-year-old has been managing a lingering lower leg and foot problem that also forced her to retire from her Cincinnati quarterfinal against Iga Swiatek in August.

Despite the setback, Rybakina recovered in time for the US Open, where she claimed her third Grand Slam title , rose to world number one and became the first player to qualify for the season-ending WTA Finals.

Rybakina is next expected to compete this month in the Ningbo Open in China, where she will try to defend her title.

The Wuhan Open is scheduled to take place from October 12 to 18.

articles.summary: El murciano evita a Djokovic y Zverev hasta la fnal del Masters 1000 chino
articles.body: Antes de saltar a disputar las semifinales del Open 500 de Tokio, Carlos Alcaraz ya supo lo que le espera en su siguiente torneo, que es el Masters 1000 de Shanghái (7 al 18). El murciano, segundo cabeza de serie y exento de la ronda inicial, se estrenará el próximo sábado 10 de octubre con el ganador del partido entre Juan Manuel Cerúndolo, el 55 del ranking ATP, y un jugador de la fase previa. En su camino aparecen Ignacio Buse (tercera ronda) y Valentin Vacherot (octavos). Cabe recordar que el monegasco es el vigente campeón del certamen. Alcaraz evita a Alexander Zverev y Novak Djokovic hasta una hipotética final. Los cabezas de serie más altos por su lado del cuadro son Daniil Medvedev (5) y Felix Auger-Aliassime (4). El ruso y el canadiense serían sus teóricos rivales en cuartos y semifinales, respectivamente. Carlitos, que se perdió la pasada edición de Shanghái por fatiga, tiene la oportunidad de sumar valiosos puntos que le afiancen en el tercer puesto de las listas. En el TMS chino regresa a la competición Ben Shelton, inmediatamente detrás de él en la clasificación. Shelton circula por la parte alta del cuadro, la misma de Zverev y Djokovic. El estadounidense sería adversario de Nole en la antepenúltima ronda. Rafa Jódar (12) y Alejandro Davidovich (25) son los otros dos españoles que aparecen como cabezas de serie. articles.standfirst: El murciano remonta un set en contra y alarga su tiranía contra tenistas españoles
articles.summary: El murciano remonta un set en contra y alarga su tiranía contra tenistas españoles
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, a sus 23 años, está a una sola victoria de desempolvar los libros de historia del Open de Tokio. El murciano se encuentra a un partido de revalidar el título y convertirse en el primer tenista que defiende la corona desde Pete Sampras (1993-94). Se le permite su victoria en la semifinal ante Jaume Munar, por 5-7, 6-3 y 6-1, en 2 horas y 31 minutos. Es la cuarta final del curso para el fenómeno de El Palmar y la primera desde que volvió tras la lesión en la muñeca. Una muestra más que el percance físico está más que olvidado. Ya son 36 finales en el circuito, el quinto español con más dentro de la Era Open. Por delante restan Rafael Nadal (131), Manuel Orantes (72), David Ferrer (52) y Carlos Moyá (44). Carlitos se une al club de Nadal y Orantes con dos últimas rondas en la capital japonesa. Su rival el martes será Jiri Lehecka, verdugo de Valentin Vacherot, por 6-4 y 6-2. Alcaraz se confirma como el gran azote de su Armada. De los 24 partidos frente a compatriotas, ha decantado 21 a su favor. Una de las tres derrotas había sido ante Munar. Pero había que remontarse a la semifinal de Marbella 2021. En ese escenario, el murciano era un tenista en formación. Ahora es un campeón de siete grandes que en Tokio se ha abonado a las remontadas. Carlitos parecía romper la semifinal con el primer break en el séptimo juego. Munar, que no se rinde nunca, no lo iba a hacer tampoco esta vez. El mallorquín perdía por 5-3 y encadenó cuatro juegos y dos roturas que le dieron el primer set. Se lo facilitaron dos dobles faltas seguidas del murciano para un total de cuatro en el parcial. "¡16 puntos seguidos! Es muy difícil jugar así", le decía a su equipo presente en la primera fila del Ariake Coliseum. El pupilo de Samuel López firmaba un 33 por ciento de puntos ganados con el segundo servicio. Por ahí se entendía la reacción de su adversario. Alcaraz se hizo con el saque de Jaume en el juego inicial de la continuación. Los dos, a su manera, se quejaban a sus banquillos por su actuación. "Atraviésala, pégale una hostia", le advertía Samu. El número tres mundial cedió por tercera vez seguida su servicio y estuvo a un punto de cederlo una cuarta. Es una realidad que se encuentra más cómodo en el resto. Desde el fondo de la pista y en la red, su tenis sí que le responde. El campeón se agarraba al cemento y situaba un favorable 3-1. Munar le exigía al máximo y recordaba la versión del tenista que llevó a España a la final de la última Copa Davis. La convocatoria para la próxima fase final de Bolonia es la más cara de la historia. Carlitos acabaría por firmar las tablas en el marcador ante el deleite de la grada. Los dos protagonistas se fueron a los vestuarios antes del asalto final para cambiar sus vestiduras. La resistencia numantina de Munar provocaría la tormenta perfecta de su condecorado contrincante. En un visto y no visto, el tanteo era de 5-0. Se quedó a las puertas del 23º rosco de su carrera. "No sé qué me pasó en el primer set, parece que me cuesta cada primer set. Pero la forma en que vuelvo me pone realmente feliz", decía el vencedor a la conclusión.

articles.summary: La polaca levanta un 6-4 y 5-2 ante Vekic y se convierte en una de las candidatas al título sin Rybakina y Sabalenka
articles.body: Iga Swiatek ejerció un claro ejercicio de supervivencia en Pekín. La tenista polaca, novena raqueta del mundo, se negó a perder hoy sobre las pistas de la capital china ante la croata Donna Vekic. Tras ir 6-4 y 5-2 abajo, completó una remontada digna de campeona (4-6, 7-6 (0) y 6-2) para clasificar a los octavos del WTA 1000 asiático. Sin Elena Rybakina y Aryna Sabalenka, multiplica sus posibilidades de repetir el título que levantó en 2023. Donna Vekic, la que fuera plata olímpica en París hace dos años, solo podía ver cómo se le escapaba el control del encuentro cada vez que le tocaba defender su servicio. Tras dominar por un set y doble 'break', solo pudo sumar tres juegos más por los 10 de su rival. Al final, la persistencia y la garra de Iga fueron lo que dictaminó la remontada. Se las verá con la joven y talentosa americana, Iva Jovic, en la ronda de las 16 mejores. Las dos primeras raquetas mundiales han caído en Pekín. Rybakina, lo hizo ante la armenia Alina Charaeva, y Sabalenka ante la checa Nikola Bartunkova. Aunque todavía presentes: Coco Gauff (4), Mirra Andreeva (5), Linda Noskova (6), Elena Svitolina (7) y Karolina Muchova (8), como jugadoras con mejor ranking, Iga Swiatek tiene por delante una oportunidad de oro para seguir escalando en la carrera por las WTA Finals en Indian Wells (8 al 15 de noviembre). Actualmente, situada en el décimo escalón de la 'race' con 3.584 puntos, a 326 de la ucraniana Marta Kostyuk, que marca el siguiente puesto. La polaca empezó su aventura sobre las pistas de Pekín en 2023. Desde ese momento, que salió como campeona en su primer intento, solo ha conocido una vez la derrota en las tres ediciones que ha disputado. Fue ante la americana Emma Navarro en 2025. Las demás ocasiones, siempre han caído del lado de la seis veces campeona de Grand Slam.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz survives first-set collapse, battles past Jaume Munar to reach Japan Open final
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz survived a major scare before finding another gear to book his place in the Japan Open final, rallying past fellow Spaniard Jaume Munar
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz survived a major scare before finding another gear to book his place in the Japan Open final, rallying past fellow Spaniard Jaume Munar 5-7, 6-3, 6-1 at the Ariake Coliseum in Tokyo on Monday.The defending champion appeared on course to close out the opening set when he led 5-3 and was serving for it. Instead, his momentum disappeared as Munar won 16 consecutive points to snatch the set and put Alcaraz under pressure. But the world No. 3 responded like a defending champion, raising his level in the second set before taking complete control in the decider to seal a two-hour, 31-minute victory.Alcaraz lets first set slipAlcaraz looked comfortable early on but could not capitalise on his 5-3 advantage. Munar broke back when the Spaniard was serving for the set and then held to move 6-5 ahead before breaking again to take the opening set.It continued a trend for Alcaraz in Tokyo, where he has been forced to dig deep in the opening sets throughout the tournament. He needed tiebreaks to get past Denis Shapovalov, Matteo Arnaldi and Alex Michelsen in the previous three rounds. Against Munar, however, there was no tiebreak comeback needed. Alcaraz had to find another route back into the contest.Seven-time Grand Slam champion shifts gearsAlcaraz immediately put the disappointment behind him in the second set. He broke for a 2-1 lead and added another break to move 4-2 ahead before securing a third break to close out the set 6-3. His first-serve effectiveness also improved, while his heavy forehand and well-timed drop shots began to unsettle Munar.The third set was almost entirely one-way traffic. Alcaraz raced to a 4-0 lead with two breaks and never allowed his compatriot to build any momentum. Munar managed to hold once, but Alcaraz calmly served out the match 6-1.Alcaraz back in a final after long layoffThe victory takes Alcaraz into his first final since returning from a four-and-a-half-month layoff caused by a right wrist injury. He also remains on course to defend the Tokyo title he won in 2025, when he defeated Taylor Fritz in the final.Alcaraz will face Czech Republic's Jiri Lehecka in the championship match after the 19th-ranked player defeated Monaco's Valentin Vacherot 6-4, 6-2 in the other semifinal.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: El ruso golpeó la pelota hacia la grada e impactó en la cara de un aficionado
articles.body: La organización del torneo de Pekín ya está tardando en levantar una estatua de Novak Djokovic en el recinto olímpico de tenis. El serbio la merece. A sus 39 años se ha plantado este lunes en su séptima final en el China Open alargando su racha de victorias hasta 33. Su última víctima ha sido Daniil Medvedev, por 7-5, 5-3 y descalificación de Medvedev tras golpear de manera fortuita a un aficionado. Habían pasado 2 horas y 29 minutos. Este martes espera Alex de Miñaur, un rival directo para entrar en las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre). El ruso, tras perder el segundo punto en el noveno juego, pegó un raquetazo a la grada, con tanta mala suerte que impactó directamente en la cara de un seguidor chino al que hizo daño. Ese es el matiz que, según la regla, provoca la descalificación de Daniil. El moscovita ya se jugó la expulsión hace dos años en la Laver Cup de Berlín por una acción similar. En esa situación nadie salió herido. El juez de silla, Mohamed Layhani, y el supervisor del torneo, hablaron antes de tomar la decisión. Djokovic vivió la misma situación en sus carnes en los octavos del US Open 2020. En su caso fue por golpear involuntariamente a una juez de línea. A Novak le ha dado igual que Medvedev llegara a la cita con siete triunfos del tirón y como campeón de Chengdu. Nole es el finalista más longevo de un certamen de categoría 500 desde su introducción en 2009. Ya son 146 veces luchando por un título, las mismas de Ivan Lendl. Por delante sólo restan Jimmy Connors (164) y Roger Federer (157). El tenista de Belgrado regresará al 'top10' mundial en la próxima actualización del ranking en detrimento de Arthur Fils. A Medvedev empezaron a entrarle todos los males tras perder su segundo saque en el ecuador del segundo set. Con 4-2, tuvo que ser atendido del hombro por parte del fisioterapeuta de la organización. Su mal carácter volvió a jugarle una mala pasada. Tim Henman, en Wimbledon 1995, Frustrado, golpeó una pelota con fuerza y le dio de lleno en la cabeza a una recogepelotas. En Queen's 2012 fue David Nalbandián el que no pudo terminar la final al golpear una valla publicitaria en la silla del juez de línea y dañarle en la rodilla. Denis Shapovalov fue descalificado de un partido de Copa Davis, en 2017, tras lanzar la bola al aire e impactar en el ojo del árbitro.

articles.title: China Open: Daniil Medvedev defaulted from Novak Djokovic match after hitting spectator with ball
articles.summary: Daniil Medvedev is defaulted from the China Open after hitting a spectator in the face with a ball during his semi-final against Novak Djokovic.
articles.body:
Daniil Medvedev was defaulted from the China Open after hitting a spectator in the face with a ball during his semi-final against Novak Djokovic.

Third seed Medvedev trailed Djokovic 7-5 5-3 when the Serb hit a winner beyond him for 15-15.

The ball ricocheted off the back of the court and Medvedev swiped at a backhand in annoyance, sending the ball into the air and hitting a spectator who was sitting in the front row of the stand behind him.

The fan doubled over holding his face and was still holding his eye as he was helped out of the arena.

After speaking with umpire Mohamed Lahyani and an ATP official, Russia's Medvedev approached the net to shake hands with Djokovic.

"Terribly sorry to the spectator, first of all," Medvedev said.

"I'm trying to get in touch with him, if he wants it. Hopefully I can apologise in person and see how he feels.

"I just hope he's OK. That's the most important. I just really care about him right now."

Djokovic - who was defaulted from the 2020 US Open for a similar incident - expressed sympathy for the fan and Medvedev afterwards.

"It's a bit of a shock to be honest. I hope that person is not badly injured," he said.

"I also feel sorry for Daniil. I know exactly how he feels to be disqualified in a big match.

"I am sure that Daniil did not want to do this intentionally."

Defaults in tennis are rare and only occur when players violate the sport's code of conduct.

Violations include ball abuse, physical or verbal abuse, or racquet abuse. Players can receive three code violations and then be disqualified if they receive another - but Medvedev's offence was serious enough to instantly default him.

He will now lose the points and prize money he had earned during his run to the last four in Beijing.

The 30-year-old is a combustible character who has struggled to control his emotions throughout his career.

He had a meltdown at last year's US Open when a photographer walked on court, and was fined almost £31,500 ($42,500) for his behaviour.

In April, he obliterated a racquet after losing 6-0 6-0 at the Monte Carlo Masters and was again fined for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Medvedev told BBC Sport in 2025 that he was attempting to work on his on-court behaviour.

"When I'm on the court I hate to lose; I love to win. My first goal is to win the match, so it brings a lot of adrenaline out and it brings all the energy out," he said.

"Sometimes it is a good energy. Sometimes it is a bad one."

Djokovic beats Zverev to reach China Open semis

'I kept fighting right to the end' - emotional Nishikori retires

The default brought an early end to an excellent contest, with 39-year-old Djokovic having played superbly to outlast an opponent nine years his junior.

Djokovic saved 16 of the 18 break points he faced and will go on to play Alex de Minaur in Tuesday's final.

Djokovic has a 33-0 record at the China Open, having won the title six times.

He has won at least one title a year since 2006 - but Tuesday will be his first final since the Australian Open, where he lost to then world number one Carlos Alcaraz in four sets.

He reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon, losing to eventual champion Jannik Sinner, but lost in the third round of the French Open before suffering a shock first-round exit at the US Open.

Elsewhere, defending champion Alcaraz overcame fluctuations in form to beat Jaume Munar and reach the Japan Open final.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion struggled on serve throughout but gradually upped his level to win 5-7 6-3 6-1.

Spain's Alcaraz led 5-3 in the first set and served for it before losing 16 consecutive points to squander the opener.

He will face Jiri Lehecka in the final after the Czech beat Monaco's Valentin Vacherot 6-4 6-2.

articles.title: Djokovic Reaches Beijing Final After Medvedev Is Defaulted For Hitting Fan
articles.summary: No. 6 Djokovic, 39, improved top a perfect 33-0 at the Beijing Open and will next face No. 5 Alex de Minaur in Tuesday’s final.
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic advanced to the Beijing Open final after his opponent Daniil Medvedev was defaulted for hitting a fan with a ball during their semifinal on Monday.

The Serbian legend was serving at 7-5, 5-3, 15-all when Medvedev hit a ball toward the stands after it had ricocheted back to him behind the baseline. The ball appeared to hit a fan in the face, and the fan was then escorted out with the help of another fan.

Under standard ATP rules for a default or disqualification during a match, Medvedev will forfeit his ranking points and prize money earned at the event.

No. 6 Djokovic, 39, improved to a perfect 33-0 at the Beijing Open and will next face No. 5 Alex de Minaur in Tuesday's final.

"A bit of a shock, to be honest," Djokovic said . "Sorry for the person [who got hit]. I honestly didn't see what happened. I hope that person is not badly injured. On the other hand, I also feel sorry for Daniil, because I know exactly how he feels to be disqualified in a big match. I was disqualified at the 2020 U.S. Open in similar circumstances. I am sure that Daniil didn't want to do this intentionally. It just happens."

In 2020, Djokovic accidentally hit a linesperson with a ball behind the baseline and was DQ'd during his fourth-round match with Pablo Careno Busta.

Prior to the incident, Djokovic and Medvedev engaged in a concussive slugfest from the baseline.

Djokovic struggled to hold serve but saved 16-of-18 break chances on his serve while converting 4-of-10 break chances against Medvedev. He broke Medvedev for 3-2 in the first set after facing several break points on his own serve.

"I was three points away from the win," Djokovic said. "It was a grueling battle and I definitely didn't want to take this level to a third set. It was looking like that. I don't know many break points I saved, it was crazy. It's always a big battle with Daniil and it's so hard to play him. When he's feeling the ball well in slower conditions with a big serve, but we move on."

De Minaur earlier advanced to his 10th ATP 500 final after Hubert Hurkacz retired from their semifinal due to an adductor injury. Hurkacz later revealed he first felt the injury during his quarterfinal win against Karen Khachanov, and the Pole was visibly hampered when he retired with De Minaur leading 6-4, 3-2.

Djokovic, who is bidding to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin, Italy, is 3-1 against de Minaur for his career.

articles.title: Shocked Novak Djokovic reacts after Daniil Medvedev is disqualified from their match in Beijing
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic was left in a state of shock after Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from their semifinal match at the China Open. Djokovic led Medvedev...
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic was left in a state of shock after Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from their semifinal match at the China Open.

Djokovic led Medvedev 7-5, 5-3 in Beijing when the Russian smashed a ball into the crowd in frustration, and it appeared to hit a spectator in the face. After a lengthy deliberation, it was decided that Medvedev would be defaulted from the match and the tournament.

ATP veteran Djokovic, who was defaulted from the 2020 US Open for hitting a line judge with a ball, has now shared his immediate reaction to the dramatic incident at the China Open . Having been in a similar situation, he understandably feels sympathy towards Medvedev.

Novak Djokovic shocked after Daniil Medvedev is disqualified from their match

Speaking in his post-match interview with the ATP Tour, Djokovic said of the incident: "A bit of a shock. I am sorry for the person, I honestly did not see what happened. I hope the person is not badly injured but on the other hand I also feel sorry for Daniil.

"I know exactly how it feels to be disqualified in a big match. I was disqualified at the 2020 US Open for similar circumstances. I am sure Daniil did not want to do this intentionally and it just happens.

"I was three points away from the win. It was a gruelling battle. I really did not want to take this to a third set. It always is a big battle with Daniil and it's so hard to play him when he is feeling the ball well in slower conditions. But we move on."

It was, of course, an accident from Medvedev, but he arguably left officials with no choice but to default him given that the ball struck a spectator. And it was a moment of madness that will have significant consequences for the Russian, who will lose his ranking points and prize money from the event. Umpire Mohamed Lahyani ultimately delivered the bad news to the Russian, who seemingly accepted his fate.

Novak Djokovic delighted to make it through tough China Open draw

Meanwhile, Djokovic will move on to yet another China Open final, as he looks to continue his flawless record at the ATP 500 tournament. He now boasts a stunning 33-0 win-loss record at the event, where he has claimed six titles.

He said ahead of another final: "I always believe in myself to be frank with you. I felt I played really well in the training session. It's different when you play an official match. My draw wasn't very favourable to be honest, played hard matches from the beginning, but it makes the run to the final sweeter. Another final, there is something about Beijing that keeps me going."

Djokovic will meet Alex de Minaur in the Beijing final, with the Australian having led Hubert Hurkacz 6-4, 3-2 in their semifinal before the Pole retired hurt. Djokovic and De Minaur have met four times throughout their careers, with the Serbian holding a 3-1 record over his rival.

The 39-year-old can be very proud of his efforts in Beijing regardless of what happens in the final, having indeed progressed through a very tricky draw. Djokovic has beaten Nuno Borges, Yunchaokete Bu, top seed Alexander Zverev and now Medvedev, who entered the event on the back of a title in Hangzhou.

articles.title: Medvedev defaulted for hitting spectator with ball
articles.summary: Daniil Medvedev is defaulted from the China Open after hitting a spectator in the face with a ball during his semi-final against Novak Djokovic.
articles.body:
Daniil Medvedev was defaulted from the China Open after hitting a spectator in the face with a ball during his semi-final against Novak Djokovic.

Third seed Medvedev trailed Djokovic 7-5 5-3 when the Serb hit a winner beyond him for 15-15.

The ball ricocheted off the back of the court and Medvedev swiped at a backhand in annoyance, sending the ball into the air and hitting a spectator who was sat in the front row of the stand behind him.

The fan doubled over holding his face and was still holding his eye as he was helped out of the arena.

After speaking with umpire Mohamed Lahyani and an ATP official, Russia's Medvedev approached the net to shake hands with Djokovic.

Djokovic - who was defaulted from the 2020 US Open for a similar incident - expressed sympathy for the fan and Medvedev afterwards.

"It's a bit of a shock to be honest. I hope that person is not badly injured," he said.

"I also feel sorry for Daniil. I know exactly how he feels to be disqualified in a big match.

"I am sure that Daniil did not want to do this intentionally."

Defaults in tennis are rare and only occur when players violate the sport's code of conducts.

Violations include ball abuse, physical or verbal abuse, or racquet abuse. Players can receive three code violations and then be disqualified if they receive another - but Medvedev's offence was serious enough to instantly default him.

He will now lose the points and prize money he had earned during his run to the last four in Beijing.

The 30-year-old is a combustible character who has struggled to control his emotions throughout his career.

He had a meltdown at last year's US Open when a photographer walked on court, and was fined almost £31,500 ($42,500) for his behaviour.

In April, he obliterated a racquet after losing 6-0 6-0 at the Monte Carlo Masters and was again fined for unsportsmanlike conduct.

Medvedev told BBC Sport in 2025 that he was attempting to work on his on-court behaviour.

"When I'm on the court I hate to lose; I love to win. My first goal is to win the match, so it brings a lot of adrenaline out and it brings all the energy out," he said.

"Sometimes it is a good energy. Sometimes it is a bad one."

The default brought an early end to an excellent contest, with 39-year-old Djokovic having played superbly to outlast an opponent nine years his junior.

The Serb was doubled over and breathing heavily as the pair engaged in long rallies, with Djokovic sliding into the splits to win a point during a 79-minute first set.

Djokovic saved 16 of the 18 break points he faced and will go on to play Alex de Minaur in Tuesday's final.

Djokovic has a 33-0 record at the China Open, having won the title six times.

He has won at least one title a year since 2006 - but Tuesday will be his first final since the Australian Open, where he lost to then world number one Carlos Alcaraz in four sets.

He reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon, losing to eventual champion Jannik Sinner, but lost in the third round of the French Open before suffering a shock first-round exit at the US Open.

articles.title: Medvedev disqualified from China Open semifinal after hitting ball and injuring member of the crowd
articles.summary: Russian Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from his China Open semifinal clash with Novak Djokovic after hitting a rebounding ball into the crowd, striking a spectator in the eye.
articles.body: Russian Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from his China Open semifinal clash with Novak Djokovic after hitting a rebounding ball into the crowd, striking a spectator in the eye. World number five Medvedev was trailing 7-5, 5-3 on Monday and had lost a point when he hit the ball coming off the wall. The spectator, who was sitting in the first row, clutched his left eye and appeared to be in pain as he walked out of the gallery, assisted by stadium staff. “I was shocked, to be honest… I hope that person is not badly injured,” said sixth seed Djokovic, who was disqualified from the US Open in 2020 under similar circumstances. “On the other hand, I also feel sorry for Daniil because I know exactly how it feels to be disqualified in a big match … I’m sure that Daniil didn’t want to do this intentionally.” Both semifinals ended prematurely in Beijing as Hubert Hurkacz retired with an adductor injury earlier on Monday. Australian Alex de Minaur was leading the first semifinal 6-4, 3-2 when his Polish opponent, who had struggled with movement throughout the match, retired.

articles.title: Daniil Medvedev defaulted for hitting spectator with ball as Novak Djokovic reaches another China Open final
articles.summary: Six-time champion Novak Djokovic moves to 33-0 at Beijing tournament after Daniil Medvedev defaulted for hitting spectator around left eye in semi-final; Medvedev to lose all points and prize money; Djokovic, who fended off 16 of the 18 break points he faced, plays Alex De Minaur in final
articles.body:
Medvedev accidentally struck the fan while trailing 7-5 5-3 and three points from defeat in Monday's punishing semi-final in Beijing, during which Djokovic saved 16 of the 18 break points he faced.

Medvedev will now lose all points and prize money eared from the event.

Djokovic, 39, won the China Open six times in seven years between 2009 and 2015 but had not returned prior to this campaign.

The Serb, who secured a come-from-behind quarter-final victory over world No 2 Alexander Zverev on Sunday, will meet Alex De Minaur in Tuesday's final as he looks to clinch a 102nd career title and first since the Hellenic Championship little under a year ago.

Speaking on court afterwards, Djokovic, defaulted at the 2020 US Open for hitting a line judge with a ball, said: "It is a bit of a shock, to be honest. I am sorry for the person.

"I didn't see what happened and I hope the person is not badly injured. I also feel sorry for Daniil as I know exactly how it feels to be disqualified in a big match.

"I'm sure he didn't want to do this intentionally."

Djokovic reached the Australian Open final in January, losing to Carlos Alcaraz in four sets, but has struggled for fitness and form since and dropped out of the world's top 10, although this run in Beijing has returned him to that elite level.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion, who has played just eight tournaments this year, revealed an ongoing medical condition that has led to fatigue and vomiting on court, with the issue exacerbated in hot and humid conditions.

Djokovic added: "It was a gruelling battle that I definitely didn't want to take to a third set. It was looking like that. It is always a big battle with Daniil, so hard to play him when he is feeling the ball in slower conditions with his big serve.

"I always believe in myself and felt I played really well in training bit obviously it is different in an official match.

"My draw wasn't favourable, very tough matches from the beginning, but it makes the run the final sweeter. Something about Beijing keeps me going."

In the women's event, Britain's Sonay Kartal saw her WTA Tour comeback end in the third round with a 6-4 6-1 loss to Alina Charaeva - the player who dumped out world No 1 Elena Rybakina at the weekend.

The Beijing event was Kartal's first WTA tournament since March after a stress fracture of the back and she picked up wins over Andrea Lazaro Garcia and Wang Xinyu before falling to Armenia's Charaeva.

Iga Swiatek , reached the fourth round after rallying from a set and 5-2 down to beat Donna Vekic 4-7 6-7 (7-0) 6-2.

articles.standfirst: El serbio se solidariza con su rival ruso, que no pudo terminar la semifinal de Pekín
articles.summary: El serbio se solidariza con su rival ruso, que no pudo terminar la semifinal de Pekín
articles.body: Novak Djokovic se benefició de la descalificación de Daniil Medvedev en las semifinales del Open 500 de Pekín y se clasificó por séptima vez en su carrera para la final del certamen de la capital china. Ya son 33 victorias por 0 derrotas en el torneo. A Djokovic se le preguntó a la conclusión sobre el incidente que había provocado la expulsión de su rival: "Siento mucho lo ocurrido a la persona que recibió el impacto; en realidad no vi qué pasó y espero que no haya sufrido lesiones. También me solidarizo con Daniil, porque sé perfectamente lo que se siente al ser descalificado durante un partido importante: a mí me ocurrió en el US Open de 2020 en circunstancias similares. Estoy seguro de que Daniil no lo hizo a propósito, pero así fue como sucedieron las cosas". Medvedev también se refirió a lo acontecido: "Lo siento. Estoy intentando ponerme en contacto con el aficionado para disculparme. Fue un accidente".

articles.title: Coco Gauff reports online racial abuse after incident during her victory over Sun Xinran at China Open
articles.summary: Coco Gauff has had to endure online racial abuse after her latest victory at the China Open; The American star beat 16-year-old Sun Xinran in straight sets though there was an incident at a key moment when Gauff had to stop a point; Gauff explained the "unfortunate situation"
articles.body:
The world No 4 won 7-5 6-1 against the 16-year-old from China to progress to the last 16 in Beijing.

Gauff was serving to stay in the first set at 4-5 when Sun thought she had hit a winner, but the American had already raised her hand to stop the point as a light in the side panels around the court was flickering.

Gauff took the next three points to hold for 5-5, and then dropped just one more game in the match.

The 22-year-old tried to explain the situation on X, saying: "It was an unfortunate situation but it is out of my control.

"Xinran is incredible talent and player, I apologised for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood."

Gauff then responded to a racist reply to her post by saying: "Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist.

"The amount of racist comments/dms I've received in the last few hours is insane.

"Lastly, I 'm not a cheater or a thief."

articles.title: China Open: Coco Gauff condemns racist abuse on social media after incident during Sun Xinran match
articles.summary: Coco Gauff says she suffered racial abuse on social media after an incident during her win over Sun Xinran at the China Open.
articles.body:
Coco Gauff says she suffered racial abuse on social media following an incident in her win over 16-year-old Sun Xinran at the China Open.

The American had been serving at 4-5 in the first set her Chinese opponent thought she had hit a winner.

However, Gauff raised her hand to halt play because of a flickering light in the side panels surrounding the court.

Gauff won the next three points to hold for 5-5 before she closed out the set, and then dropped just one game in the remainder of the contest as she claimed a 7-5 6-1 victory to reach the last 16 in Beijing.

The world number four gave a lengthy explanation of why she stopped the point in a post on X and said it was "an unfortunate situation" but "out of my control", adding that Sun had understood and accepted her apology.

Gauff then responded to a reply to her original post which included racist language.

"You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff wrote.

"The amount of racist comments/direct messages I've received in the last few hours is insane. Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief."

Gauff is far from the first player in the women's game to suffer social media abuse.

A report in July said female players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media in 2025.

The WTA and World Tennis said "collective action" was required to make "significant progress" in tackling abuse.
